headline: Musk says Google has ‘expressed interest’ in renting more AI computing power from SpaceX
author: Ford McCracken

paragraphs.text: Elon Musk suggested Saturday that Google could rent additional compute from SpaceX data centers as demand for AI power continues to increase.

In a post to his social platform, X, Musk replied to a post from a user with whom he frequently interacts. The account suggested Google could buy more AI computing power from SpaceX, even more than other companies like Anthropic, to power its Gemini AI models, which are now also used in Apple products.
“Not sure who will buy more, but Google has expressed interest in renting more compute from us,” Musk wrote.

Musk’s space exploration, media and AI company is rapidly expanding the industry by constructing new data centers and renting compute to other firms. SpaceX recently announced it would build a new data center in South Texas, near its headquarters in Starbase. It also committed to generating its own power and expanding the local water supply.

As demand for compute to power AI models surges, SpaceX is building data centers faster than many competitors. A facility it constructed in Memphis was operational in just 122 days, according to Barron‘s, and reached its planned capacity in 276 days.

Both Google and Anthropic continue to spend more on compute, with both companies paying SpaceX billions under current agreements. Google pays SpaceX more than $800 million a month, and Anthropic pays more than $3 billion monthly to rent compute. Anthropic’s models, like others on the market, have usage limits to constrain demand.

The data center buildout may face increased scrutiny with Democrats preparing to reclaim the majority in Congress. Several Democratic candidates throughout the country campaigned on significantly restricting data centers or halting projects entirely as public opinion continues to sour on the facilities.

While markets initially dipped after Democrats’ sweeping midterm victories, fears over data center restrictions triggered a stock market selloff even before Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation caused another downturn in tech and AI stocks. His return caused Nvidia’s stock to at least partially bounce back. Both SpaceX and Anthropic debuted initial public offerings on the stock market this year, worth well over $1 trillion each.
